prompt: Your friend has been offered a place on a course at the university where you studied. He/She would like your advice about finding a place to live. Write an email to your friend. In your email * describe where you lived when you were a student at the university * recommend the best way for him/her to look for accomodation * warn him/her of mistakes students make when choosing accommodation
essay:
Dear Myat Noe,

I hope you are well. I'm so pleased that you have been offered an Industrial and Operations Management course at Republic Polytechnic Singapore, where I have attended for three years. Personally, I'd like to suggest that you  find the right place to accommodate yourself while you are studying there, as I have some prior experience in Singapore.

To begin with, it's better to stay close to campus, located in the Woodlands area, where I used to share a room with a friendly Indonesian roommate, because it will reduce your public transportation fees effectively. At that time, the rental cost was S$500 per month , including Wifi and utility bills, and I had to pay S$300 deposit to the Singaporean landlord. 

In addition, it's so important that you should find the appropriate one by surfing the trusted property websites such as www.singaporehousing.com or www.sgfindhouse.com, where you can see the competitive fees in different facilities of apartments, and make up your mind on the correct one after observing them in reality. 

However, you should be aware that estate agents can confuse you about the make-up information about the rooms. In my point of view, I prefer looking at the data of reviews of residents posted in google map and Facebook media before checking the place with representatives.Last, be careful of some misleading errors because of low price, they can be costly in other facilities like MRT train and bus fares, and even you may meet with bad landlords or safety might not be ascertained.

Hope you could find some ideas in my letter. Anyway, so glad for your ambition to study there.

With love,

Swe Zin Moe
